The gameplay is...alright, I guess. Graphics and sound are...adequate for the time.

The writing is what takes this from "kinda meh" to "avoid at all costs".

The characters are all idiots, and what's worse is they're [i]inconsistent[/i] idiots who apparently change their whole personality every five minutes so that they can pick the dumbest possible thing to do at any given moment. Whenever one shows occasional flashes of likeability they immediately turn around and ruin it with the very next thing that comes out of their mouths. The plot is "I am 14 and this is my first-ever DnD campaign!" levels of generic and the humor, well...either something went [i]seriously[/i] wrong in translation or whoever originally wrote those "jokes" is suffering from some kind of serious issues. Possibly both.


Verdict: Play literally [i]any[/i] other Tales Of... game instead.

I was a big fan of Berseria and wanted to like this. About 10hrs in I was struggling to find a reason to start the game again. A few complaints:

- Locked chests in dungeons with the key located in a different dungeon. Just...why? Backtracking for 1-2 chests is extremely anti-fun.
- Camera can be wonky and get stuck in odd spots during combat.
- Forced to complete side quests to advance main story. Just a lazy attempt to make the game longer.
- Combat doesn't feel satisfying. Different combos and artes really don't make an impact. Pretty much comes down to spamming the same 3-4 attack combos,
- Tuned heavily with focus around armatization. Characters later on die to bosses with 1-2 hits if you're not armatized. No ability to be tactical later just armatize and go.

Go play Berseria instead. It's the best Tales experience.

I've heard good things about the stories and this one in particular had a short anime that my favorite band played the OP for.  4 hours in and I was overwhelmed with the amount of micromanaging you have to do with gear/shops/skills.  7 hours in and those things still hadn't been explained and the game carries on like the devs couldn't care less how confusing they made their entire interface?
What to fight well?  Switch to Manual or Semi-auto and watch as your combos fail because the input for each attach has such fails to register.  Switch to Auto and watch as your characters make you feel like a trash player, but now you can't issue strategic commands to your party.  I've beaten all three Dark Souls and Bloodborne, and yet THIS was somehow harder.  And for a JRPG where planning ahead with gear and grinding is kinda the point, that is a game-breaking flaw.
I will not be playing games from this series ever again.  I had fun during the prolog, but the amount of things they expect you to put up with just to progress is ridiculous.  2/10, watch others play before you buy. and only buy on sale if you really want to give it a shot.  Good luck.

Я прошел очень много разных японских рпг, но эта часть удивила меня. Я просто вахуе, насколько в этой игре идеальное вербальное и невербальное взаимодеиствие персонажей. Они проработали каждую мимику лица, каждое движение тела. Впитали буквально в любое деиствие свой смысл и логику. Игра состоит из миллиарда мелочей движения тела. И это я еще не говорю об озвучке: о том, что говорит персонаж и о чем  думает. Я просто в шоке, насколько в игре реалистичное взаимодеиствие персонажей. Они создали не просто болванчиков, которые стоят на месте в карикатурных позах и каменной мимикой, а воссоздали реальные взаимодеиствия людей. 
Я еще и по другим частям понял, что они могут во взаимодеиствие и характеры, но тут у меня просто отвисла челюсть. 
Вау. Просто вaxуе. И мне больно видеть ее оценки в стиме. История -  шикарная; персонажи - идеальные; взаимодеиствие - лучшее, что я видел во множестве других японских рпг. Но оценки низкие. Я могу понять людей, почему оценки низкие, но я все равно не согласен. Игра очень глубокая. Каждый персонаж - не просто личность, а eбaный кремень, просто нефритовый стержень. Игра хоть и подается очень по-детски, с инфантильными нотами, но события и происходящее вокруг - вообще не детские. Рост персонажей, их чувства, деиствия и выборы - вау. Игра просто кайф. Утомительной беготни дoпiзды, но боевка и сюжет раскрываются через 30% игры (как обычно в теилсах), так что норм. 

Я очень доволен игрой. Персонажи серии Tales всегда выделялись самобытными личностями, которые не являются "подпевалами главного героя". Каждый персонаж в игре - личность, со своими убеждениями и волей, чего нет в большинстве японских рпг: будто ff (не все), trails, ys, персоны и других менее известных серий игр. Ты чувствуешь это сразу - и за это я и люблю эту серию игр. Персонажи и сюжет целиком перекрыли устарелый (даже на момент выхода игры) геймплей. Я считаю взаимодеиствие персонажей в игре - эталоном, на кой должны ровняться все другие.

Zestiria как раз второй случай.
Здесь плохо буквально всё. Техническая часть, сюжет, персонажи, наполнение мира, музыка и т.д.
Самая важная составляющая боевая система реализована настолько криво, что, кажется, любой выпускник бесплатных курсов программирования справился бы лучше и ещё добавил бы пару уникальных механик от себя.
Сюжет настолько скучный и неинтересный, что, по сути, это даже не главная проблема игры, всё остальное сделано ещё хуже.
Персонажи просто никакие. Из всей компании хоть какой-то интерес представляют Роза, Дензел, Алиша и Эдна. У первых двух есть свои мотивы (наверное ((надеюсь)) ). Алиша берёт на себя ответственность за происходящее в своей стране, что хотя бы говорит о наличии характера (в отличие от того же Сорея). Но самое тупое, её после первых часов игры просто убирают из основной группы, и дальше она существует где-то на фоне, практически не участвуя в сюжете. Эдна же вызывает интерес в основном потому, что она сестра Айзена из Berseria (одного из лучших персонажей всей серии Tales).
Сорей пустышка. Он не то что рядом с Велвет (главной героиней Berseria) не стоит, он даже по соседней улице с ней не проходил. Миклео и Лайла вообще картонные персонажи. Один только Рокуро из Berseria превосходит весь основной каст Zestiria по уровню проработки и вложенной души.
Мир игры настолько же большой, насколько и пустой. Быстрое перемещение доступно не всегда, поэтому вам часто придётся бегать по пустым локациям и нервно отвлекаться на телефон.
Музыка это то, что иногда может спасти даже провальную игру но здесь тоже не вытягивает. Она пресная, скучная и совершенно не запоминается. Особенно это заметно на фоне Berseria, где саундтрек отлично дополняет и экшен, и эмоциональные моменты. Единственный ost, который действительно вызывает эмоции это тема Завейда.

Итог: НЕ ПОКУПАЙТЕ ЭТО. Если хотите познакомиться с серией Tales, начните с Berseria. Она значительно лучше по всем параметрам и, самое главное, подарит вам интересную и запоминающуюся историю.

Tales of Zestiria is one of those JRPGs that feels frustrating more often than it feels rewarding. The combat system is stiff and awkward, lacking the fluidity you would expect, and the battle camera frequently gets in the way, making fights harder to read and enjoy. Encounters happen too often, turning exploration into a repetitive and exhausting loop. The level design does not help either, as areas feel similar and uninspired, which only amplifies the sense of repetition. On top of that, the world itself feels empty, with large spaces that offer very little meaningful interaction.

The issues extend into progression and storytelling as well. The story comes across as flat and fails to build strong emotional engagement, making it difficult to stay invested. Quest objectives are often unclear, leaving players confused about what to do next. At times, the game forces players to explore or complete side activities just to progress the main story, including collecting specific items without clear guidance. This design choice feels less like meaningful exploration and more like artificial padding, making the overall experience feel unnecessarily tedious rather than engaging.

Если Berseria — это ярость, стиснутая в кулак, то Tales of Zestiria — это почти сказание у костра: история о чистоте, вере и попытке сохранить свет в мире, который медленно заражается злобой. Steam-описание прямо подаёт игру как путешествие Сорея по средневековому фэнтези-миру, а визуальный стиль с роликами ufotable действительно делает её похожей на ожившую легенду.

В Zestiria попадаешь не как в мрачную трагедию, а как в большое странствие, где важнее не шок и жестокость, а чувство дороги. Поля, руины, города и святилища создают ощущение мира, который хочется не просто пройти, а именно прожить, и даже критики отмечали в игре уютное чувство приключения и яркий, почти классический fantasy-настрой.

Главная сила Zestiria — в том, как она соединяет традиционный дух JRPG с очень подвижной боевой системой. На странице Steam подчёркиваются бесшовные сражения без отдельных экранов загрузки и слияние Сорея с Серафимами; в обзоре RPG Site именно боевая система названа тем местом, где игра раскрывается лучше всего. Это делает каждый бой не просто обменом ударами, а моментом, где тактика и зрелищность наконец начинают работать вместе.

Особенно запоминается ощущение, когда путешествие вдруг перестаёт быть просто “ещё одной JRPG” и начинает работать как настоящее сказание о взрослении героя. Сорей не выглядит персонажем, который ломает мир о колено; он скорее пытается выдержать его вес, не потеряв доброту. Именно поэтому Zestiria цепляет не драматизмом на разрыв, а мягкой, упрямой верой в то, что свет всё ещё имеет значение. Это не самая дерзкая Tales, но одна из самых искренних.

Pretty poor Tales game and I've only played Berseria and Vesperia. I think the one good trait this game has is the chemistry and banter between the cast but that goes for any Tales game. 

We have generic naive good guy, Sorey, as our main character tasked with saving the world from bad guys. That's it. There is no character complexity like in Berseria with Velvet being sort of the perceived villain and completely filled with the desire for revenge. Or like Yuri, the vigilante, going about delivering justice in his own way. No. Sorey is just from the start, Mr. Goody Two Shoes and thats it. 

Combat is a downgrade from Berseria. The battles take place wherever you initiated the fight so you end up fighting on sloped hills or claustrophobic areas where the camera just gets stuck looking at the ground and other janky stuff. Not that Berseria's gameplay was that great to begin with. 

The overworld is just a whole lot of empty space and a lot of running.

And this game runs at 30fps by default somehow. Had to install a mod just to get 60fps.

Honestly embarrassingly bad for a game made by a professional studio. I don't like to abandon things so quickly but absolutely everything about ToZ just screams "avoid me" like a poison dart frog. The entire thing reeks of cheapness. I can't find any real information on it online but this whole debacle must have been rushed out, or given a bad budget, or a team of people new to the industry, or something. I really hope there was some excuse, cause the alternative is just sad.

The most noticeable thing here is that the game is just butt ugly- I'm not usually the type to really get on something for "graphical fidelity" and play the "but in X year there should be Y HD-ness" card, but it really does just boggle the mind how the company behind games like Tales of Symphonia, Vesperia, even Legendia could produce something that looks like a low budget, early days PS2 game (discounting the character models). There was a smash cut early in the game from a cutscene to an enormous, perfectly straight, low poly hallway bridge on a flat environment that actually made me lose my composure and burst out laughing. It's that bad.

The world is just flat, sparse, and drab- something that carries over to the characters, who all animate like stiff robots or marionette dolls while spewing out some of most amateurish writing I've seen in a professional production in a long time. Sure, Tales games can be a bit hit or miss with the characters sometimes, but this is just embarrassing. It reads like something written by a teenager for a school project, and isn't helped by being backed by the blandest "big evil guy and the destined hero" rubbish in the world. A story brief that was old 20 years before this game game out.

Mechanically the game feels like a very new-school RPG, full of button mashing, caked in stupid flash and flair, with jumbled piles of excessive gimmicky system nonsense lobbed at you in a big, useless, impossible to digest pile before you have a chance to acclimate to even the most basic parts of the game. Even hours in I was still getting tutorial prompts in almost every battle about yet another tacked on piece of nonsense the battles featured. Like they believed if they crammed enough crap in there it'd make it worthwhile to play, instead of just having a solid base to work something unique on top of.

Also, you know, gotta love the new-school thing where characters won't ever shut the ♥♥♥♥ up during combat OR exploration. How about instead of just bad characters, we have bad characters who you always have to listen to, yapping about total garbage 24/7, because god forbid the modern gamer doesn't have a button to mash, a big flashy animation to gawk at, or a quip to hear every ten seconds.

Maybe the characters and the plot get better later on, but why would I stick around for it? The game is grating to listen to, annoying to play, and obnoxious to look at. ToZ is the type of game that just gives you a sense of "you only have so many years to live- why spend those hours, those days, dealing with something so laughably, pathetically bad?

Took a while.  A lot of false starts and stops over the years.

Opinion has not changed.  Zestiria is blatantly overhated, and unreasonably so.  This is where we explain.

[H1]Three Elements, Three Different Opinions[/H1]
[hr][/hr]
[olist]
[*]Cutscenes/graphics
[*]Gameplay/Combat/Controls
[*]Story/Plot/Characters
[/olist]

Players of this game have chosen one of these, and disregarded the others.  That's because for whatever reason, we got to a point where people stopped caring about good stories and characters and only care about fighting.  Which then causes them to get bored easily and complain about the games being too short/easy/etc.  Which then causes the game shops to pay less attention to quality in games, because of catering to the ADHD of it all.  Which then causes them to shut down when they don't make as much money.

Games must have ALL THREE of the attributes mentioned.  But a game that has a "meh" battle engine is still workable if it's got endearing characters, a compelling story, a well-built world, great graphics, great music, etc.  Case-in-point: Arc Rise Fantasia.

Those that claim Zestiria is the "worst" Tales game, only care about the second bullet up there.  Frankly, Vesperia is nowhere near as fluid as this one in that regard yet people think it's the greatest (it really isn't).  Besides, everyone knows the worst tales game is Symphonia, and it's not close.

If we had to list a negative, it's simply that it feels disconnected from Berseria, the canon prequel to the events here.  It feels like there's a game missing in the middle of these two, and as a result, it's slightly difficult to connect the dots up.  Very similar feeling to "Tales of Aionios" (aka Xenoblade Chronicles 3's base game) where the only real connection is by way of observed landmarks, rather than direct callbacks, because so much time passed in between.  Eizen (from Berseria) has a whole experience that you never see, not even in flashbacks.  It's annoying.

Much was said about the abruptness with how Alisha was treated.  It's abrupt, but it's clear they were trying to write her a specific way that just came off awkward.  The DLC (which we missed the free of, and thus can't justify the paid version of) was an attempt to placate, but ended up pissing people off even more.  We liked Alisha, but it's true that she felt out-of-place as a main character.

But when you get to the almost-final boss and he flashes a bit of a "whoa" moment, that was excellently done.  Haven't felt that sort of impact in a game's story in a very long time.

Is it the "best" Tales game?  Absolutely not.  That honor still remains with Tales of the Abyss.  But it's better than Vesperia, Berseria, Legendia, Symphonia and definitely Arise by a WIDE margin.  Again, as an overall story and experience, NOT just the battle engine.

І все одно що навпроти тебе може стояти хлоп, який зарізав всю твою сім'ю, адже тепер ви друзі! Вловлюєте що я маю на увазі? Щоб ви не подумали що я хейтер, ось цей описаний перехід від ворогів до друзяшок відбувається ОДНОМОМЕНТНО! Майже нічого не тягнуло до такого переходу, ви просто в одни момент споглядаєте результат японського "генія", який подумав: "О так, саме так і сталося б у гарному сюжеті".
 Сюжет пропетляли, тепер про персонажів. Головний герой, Сорей, бездарний шмат коду. Головна особливість Сорея у його відчуженності від конфліктів людей, тобто людина посередині. Як це реалізовано? Ніяк. Прогресія персонажа? Розробники про таке слово не чули. Єдина прогресія це ваша ненависть до персонажа. ... Сам гг не є якоюсь мері с'ю, але його існування та конфлікти у грі є несумісними, цей персонаж не здатен передати відчуття свідка конфлікту, що там вже казати про його учасника. А що там другорядними персонажами? Уявіть собі, другорядні персонажі відчуваються живішими за гг, а так не має бути. Чому коротенька сюжетка, з купою дірок, персонажа є цікавішою за оповідку про головного героя? Напевно самі тільки сценаристи знають відповідь. 
 Буде некоректно порівнювати сюжет Зестірії з Берсерією, так як перша вийшла пізніше другої, та оповідає історію після, коли як Берсерія (в потугах) штопає дірки своєї ігрової попередниці, але попри те помітно, як сильно відрізняється сюжет обох ігор в плані підходу до історії. 
 В заключенні просто додам, що Зестірія, як історія, намагається зачіпати політику. Але настільки бездарної реалізації я ще не бачив у своєму житті. І хотілося б сподіватися що ніколи не побачу гірше.

I honestly don’t know where to begin with Tales of Zestiria. In my view, it stands as the weakest entry in the series by a wide margin. That isn’t a statement I make lightly, especially as someone who enjoys the Tales formula. But nearly every core pillar that makes this franchise compelling: writing, combat, progression, and character presentation feels mishandled here.

The most glaring issue is the writing. It feels inconsistent, unfocused, and at times shockingly amateurish. The lore establishes rules and thematic ideas that it either forgets or contradicts later. The narrative tone shifts erratically: scenes that should carry emotional weight are brushed past without giving the player time to feel them, while lighter or humorous moments are treated with unnecessary seriousness. There’s no clear tonal throughline. Instead of building momentum or thematic cohesion, the story often feels like a collection of loosely connected beats that don’t meaningfully reinforce each other. As a result, character arcs lack impact, and major story developments fail to land with the gravitas they aim for.

Loot and progression are another major disappointment. In most RPGs, acquiring new equipment feels rewarding it signals growth, experimentation, or optimization. In Zestiria, loot often feels disposable and uninspired. Gear drops rarely generate excitement because the system surrounding equipment skills and fusion is unintuitive and tedious rather than satisfying. Instead of looking forward to new items, I frequently found myself ignoring them, which undermines a fundamental reward loop that RPGs rely on.
Combat, which should be the series’ strong suit, also struggles. While Tales games are often praised for their fluid action-based systems, here combat can feel clunky and awkward. Movement lacks smoothness, positioning can be frustrating, and fights often devolve into button mashing rather than strategic engagement. Enemy behavior sometimes adds to this frustration instances where foes become invulnerable or difficult to meaningfully interact with lack clear visual communication, which makes encounters feel arbitrary rather than challenging. Instead of feeling skill-based, combat can feel messy and unresponsive.

The voice acting is inconsistent as well. Some performances are passable, but others lack emotional nuance or energy, which only compounds the issues with the writing. When the script already struggles to carry dramatic moments, uneven delivery further weakens the impact.

That said, the game is not without merit. The soundtrack is genuinely strong, and the audio design overall is one of its few standout qualities. There are tracks that elevate scenes beyond what the writing accomplishes on its own. Additionally, the game is relatively stable from a technical standpoint. Bugs and performance issues are minimal, which at least allows the experience to be smooth in terms of functionality.

Ultimately, Tales of Zestiria feels like a game with solid foundational ideas that were poorly executed. It lacks the narrative cohesion, engaging combat flow, and rewarding progression systems that define the best entries in the franchise. While it has flashes of quality, particularly in its music, it never comes together into a satisfying whole.

[h1][b]🎮 Reseña de Tales of Zestiria[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Tales of Zestiria es un [b]JRPG de acción[/b] con estética anime y fantasía “luminosita”, donde te venden la idea de un héroe elegido (sí, otra vez) que va a “purificar” el mundo mientras colecciona compañeros, habilidades y excusas para pelear cada 30 segundos. Es un rol japonés que mezcla exploración tipo aventura, combate en tiempo real y un enfoque fuerte en la narrativa… cuando se acuerda de tener ritmo.

La primera impresión es clara: [b]banda sonora potente[/b], mundo con vibra atmosférica y un sistema de combate que quiere verse espectacular. Y lo logra… hasta que te das cuenta de que también quiere ser profundo, balanceado y legible. Spoiler: a ratos se le olvida.

Además, trae opciones de [b]cooperativo local / pantalla compartida[/b] (y Remote Play Together), ideal para discutir con un amigo sobre quién arruinó la pelea: tú, él o la IA con complejo de poeta.

[h2]Lo Serafín y lo Maldito[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
✅ 🎵 Gran banda sonora: de esas que te hacen perdonar decisiones cuestionables… por unos minutos.  
✅ 🎮 Compatibilidad total con mando: como debe ser en un JRPG de acción.  
✅ 🤝 Cooperativo local / multijugador: perfecto para convertir combates en caos coordinado.  
✅ ☁️ Steam Cloud + logros (56): para presumir progreso y también tus malas decisiones.  
✅ 🌍 Fantasía con buena trama (cuando despega): tiene momentos que sí te atrapan.

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 🧠 IA / dificultad irregular: a veces sientes que el juego pelea contigo, no contra ti.  
❌ 🗺️ “Mundo abierto” con asterisco: se siente más como “espacios amplios para correr” que libertad real.  
❌ ⚔️ Combate vistoso pero no siempre claro: entre efectos y movimiento, a ratos es “fe, esperanza y botones”.  
❌ 🎭 Tono narrativo inconsistente: pasa de épico a “anime de domingo” sin pedir permiso.  
❌ 👥 Comunidad pequeña (43 jugadores): no es que esté muerto… digamos que está meditando.

Tales of Zestiria es como ese anime que recomiendas con una condición: “mira, aguanta los primeros episodios y luego se pone bueno”. Ahora, seamos polémicos: con [b]7087 recomendaciones[/b], claramente hizo algo bien… pero con [b]43 jugadores activos[/b], también queda claro que no todos se quedaron a vivir aquí. Es un juego para fans del rol japonés y la fantasía que disfrutan el viaje aunque el camino tenga baches narrativos y peleas donde la IA se cree protagonista.

i have mixed feelings about zestiria. a decade later i finally decided to play it, and while i don't think it's the biggest pile of garbage some people depict it to be, the game can be very easy described as "average and toothless"

the first big issue is the areas. instead of going for more impact but smaller locations, every place was made to fit transitions into battles in real time/locations. and the result? locations suck. there's nothing going on in huge zones purely made to accomodate a handful of enemies at a time. but being from 2015 and so an era where "immersion" was a thing that was being expanded in gaming, this is not really surprising. unfortunately, most of it is a wash, because they sacrificed what made most tales of games interesting in the first place (smaller more constrained world that left more to your imagination by making what you could explore memorable) by going for this approach.

on top of that, it does not help that the game does not stop throwing tutorials your way. even several hours in, you will regularly get tutorials. and not even interesting ones for new, unlocked systems but basic stuff like "hey did you know you have a map?" because they forgot about it and decided that shoving a monolith with a basic tutorial 6 hours in was a good idea. the game never ever trusts you.

and the cherry on top of this not-so-great sundae is the combat. it's not very good! there's tons of systems in the game but none of them feel like they matter. even on normal, which could get tricky in other tales of games, this one just kinda lets you cruise control through everything. why should you bother to learn about how to properly use anything if there's very little punishment for not interacting with any system properly (SC, artes, armatizes, equipment fusion, skills and so on) at all?

there is more to talk about but i don't really feel like it. i don't think there's anything wrong with wanting to play this game or considering picking it up, but for most it's a safe skip and for the rest this is a 'on sale' game. there are better games, especially in the tales of series, widely available that are more worth your time.
